FSS are planar periodic structures composed of identical conducting patches or apertures arranged in one or two-dimensional arrays
The paper was published in Progress In Electromagnetics Research B, Vol. 38, 2012
Research was conducted at Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee by authors from Electronics and Computer Engineering and Metallurgical and Materials Engineering departments
Eight ferrite materials were evaluated in the material database for optimization
The target frequency range for optimization was 8-12 GHz (X-band)
Genetic Algorithm was used as the primary optimization technique due to its capability to handle large numbers of variables
The Equivalent Circuit method was selected for FSS analysis as it is simple and powerful
Five different FSS configurations were analyzed: Single Square Loop, Double Square Loop, Triple Square Loop, Cross Dipole, and Jerusalem Cross
Ba(MnTi)Fe₁.₆₈.₈O₁₉ was selected as the optimal ferrite material from the database
Bare ferrite coating achieved only 0.58 dB maximum absorption at 10.5 and 11 GHz
Single Square FSS achieved 2 dB maximum absorption at 9 GHz and 10.5 GHz
Double Square FSS achieved 4.99 dB maximum absorption at 10 GHz
Triple Square FSS achieved 9.19 dB maximum absorption at 10 GHz
Cross Dipole FSS achieved 5.22 dB maximum absorption at 9 GHz
Jerusalem Cross FSS achieved 4.86 dB maximum absorption at 9 GHz and 10.5 GHz
The ferrite coating thickness was optimized to 0.2 mm for all samples
Photolithographic method followed by wet etching was used for FSS fabrication
Copper foil was used as the conducting material for FSS patches
An Absorption Testing Device (ATD) was developed specifically for measuring absorption at 8-12 GHz
Test samples were 2 mm thick aluminum sheets with dimensions 94.5 × 74.2 mm²
The ferrite paint was dried for 8-10 hours before FSS fabrication
The complete FSS-RAM structure was dried for 48 hours after assembly
Triple square FSS showed the most significant enhancement in absorption compared to other configurations
Implementation of FSS on RAM coating reduces the overall thickness of radar absorbers
The study demonstrates that proper material and FSS dimension selection can significantly improve absorption efficiency
